title: Tiered intake and SLA routing for console reporting requests
creator: Jordan Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit a wide variety of console/reporting requests (ad-hoc usage exports, per-tenant cost breakdowns, scheduled dashboards, and high-cardinality drilldowns). Our current manual triage path causes delayed SLAs, inconsistent effort estimation, and missed signals for high-risk export requests (PII, large-scale extracts).

Goal: Implement a tiered intake and automated routing system for console reporting requests that classifies requests into pre-defined lanes (self-serve, scheduled export, engineering-assisted delivery, legal/security review) based on form inputs and telemetry signals. The system should provide clear SLA expectations, estimated effort, and an automated escalation path for requests flagged as sensitive or high-cost.

Scope: Build a new intake form and backend triage classifier, add routing rules in the Console intake workflow, instrument telemetry signals (workspace usage volume, recent export frequency, token costs, requester tier), and create clear SLAs and owner assignments for each lane. The initial rollout will cover US and EU workspaces and prioritized enterprise accounts only.
acceptance_criteria: New intake form deployed in Console that captures structured fields: request type, desired cadence, export format, sample dataset, stakeholder, tenant scope, estimated date range, and sensitivity flags.
Automated triage engine classifies >= 85% of incoming requests into one of four lanes (self-serve, scheduled-export, eng-assisted, legal-review) in pilot group compared to manual baseline.

Each lane has documented SLA: self-serve (0-2 business days auto-respond), scheduled-export (5 business days onboarding + scheduled cadence), eng-assisted (SLA window + initial scope call within 3 business days), legal-review (escalate within 1 business day).
Console shows estimated effort (S/M/L) and expected delivery window to requester immediately after submission.
Sensitive exports (PII, >100M rows, cross-tenant joins) are automatically flagged and blocked pending security approval; audit log entries created for each blocked request.
Routing rules and telemetry scoring function are documented in Confluence and can be reviewed by Product, Security, and Support teams.
Pilot run (30 days) demonstrates a 30% reduction in manual routing work for Support and 20% faster median time-to-first-response for enterprise reporting requests.
notes_and_updates: 2025-11-12: Initial intake created after recurring stakeholder sync (Support, Sales, Security). Captured common failure modes: ambiguous request scope, missing dataset samples, unclear SLA expectations.

2025-12-05: Product + Eng kickoff. Agreed minimum viable lanes: self-serve exports, scheduled exports, engineering assistance, legal/security review. Engineering to prototype classifier based on form + telemetry signals.

2026-01-22: Prototype triage classifier v0 implemented (feature branch: feature/triage-scorer). Uses signals: workspace_daily_query_volume, avg_token_cost_last_30d, past_export_frequency, account_tier. Early accuracy ~72% on labelled backlog sample (n=420).
2026-02-09: Design review — in-progress intake UI mockups added to link; UX requested clearer examples for 'sensitivity' field and inline guidance on sample dataset formatting.
2026-02-25: Security flagged requirement for export size caps and enforced redact/transform patterns for tenant-level extracts. Security review kickoff scheduled.

2026-03-02: Decision: iterate classifier with simple threshold rules + allow human override. Rationale: lower initial complexity, transparent routing, easier audit. Follow-up: add ML re-ranker in Q3 if metrics justify.
2026-03-08: Pilot cohort defined: 15 enterprise customers (sales-nominated) + internal Support requests. Support playbook drafted and linked.
2026-03-10: Updated acceptance targets and added estimated effort display requirement. Assigned Priya as PM lead to coordinate pilot.
